findings.summary: The new per-check Minor finding goes ahead of the verifier's findings. display.rs prints only the first five, so verifier Blocker/Major findings can drop out of the owner's view.
findings.evidence: In `judge` the per-check Athena findings come first (verify.rs:448-471). Then come the Major 'Behavior criterion N is unmet' findings (verify.rs:599). The verifier's own findings are added last (verify.rs:615-624). display.rs:985 runs `for finding in v.findings.iter().take(5)` for a Rejected job. Today a failing `test` check adds at most one Minor finding ('newly failing'). With this plan, each failing check can add a second one, for example clippy's `--> crates/...` lines plus test panics. Three failing checks could fill five slots with Athena Minor notes. The Dependents entry says display.rs is 'covered by the whole-job test', but that test only asserts the finding is in `done.verification.findings`. It never checks what the owner is shown or that the verifier's findings are still shown. Fix: Do not put the finding ahead of the others. Either append the path findings after the verifier's findings (push them after verify.rs:615-633), or fold the path and route text into the existing per-check 'newly failing' Minor finding so each check still has at most one. Add a test, for example in verify.rs, where a verdict has a failing check with cited paths and a verifier Blocker finding, and assert that the Blocker comes within the first five findings. Update the display.rs Dependents entry to name that test.
findings.location: Plan step 4 (push in the `blocking_checks` loop after verify.rs:471); Dependents entry for crates/athena-cli/src/display.rs:985

findings.summary: The route facts are emitted only when a tracked path is cited, though the plan calls them the part that separates cases.
findings.evidence: Decision 2 and the Risks say 'The route sentence is the part that separates cases.' Yet step 4 gives no finding at all when no tracked path is cited. That covers a 200-line tail that cut off the panic line (checks.rs:186), a build error, absolute paths, and a fmt diff that prints absolute paths. In those cases the verifier and the owner do not learn whether the same check passed on the base, or that no usable baseline existed. The reading's 'failures with no paths yield no finding' applies to the path mapping. The route facts are something the plan added. Fix: Emit the route sentence for every blocking failed check, and add the path clauses only when `failure_paths` lists something. Or record in D186 why the route is left out when no path is cited. Add a case to the criterion 3 test for a failing check with no cited path.
findings.location: Plan step 4 (`failure_path_finding` returns None when `failure_paths` lists nothing); Decision 2

findings.summary: The change description replaces criterion 1's 'concurrent change' wording with 'a change in the tested tree', and the verifier may not see it as matching.
findings.evidence: Criterion 1 requires the description to say that 'a failure from a concurrent change is indistinguishable from the job's own'. The plan's CHANGELOG and D186 sentence says 'a failure from a change in the tested tree is not told apart from the job's own'. It also argues that a later merge cannot enter the tested tree: the baseline is checked against `b.base_commit == p` (verification.rs:51-54), and `merge_tree` is used only for a stale resume (run/mod.rs:681-703). The argument is sound, but the text no longer says what the criterion asks for. Fix: Keep the criterion's phrase and add the correction. State that a concurrent change can reach the tested tree only by being in the base. When a usable baseline exists, that case is already pre-existing. Without one, the finding says 'no usable baseline'. Then the description both meets criterion 1 and fixes the old note.
findings.location: Demonstration for criterion 1; Approach (correction of CHANGELOG.md:1652-1653)

findings.summary: The CHANGELOG entry goes under 'Added', but the change fixes a gap in an existing feature.
findings.evidence: The earlier entry on the same failure class (CHANGELOG.md:1644-1653) describes a fix at the comparison. This change is the follow-up to the case that entry left out. Fix: Put the entry under Fixed, or under whatever section the earlier root-cause entries in [Unreleased] use.

summary: The plan matches the request and the reading. It adds no refusal rule and gives the verdict and the verifier brief the information that was missing. The places it changes are where the gap starts: `judge`'s blocking-check loop at verify.rs:447-472, and `check_result_view` at verify.rs:62-88, which gives no tail for a check Athena ran itself. I read that the verifier always runs (verification.rs:187), that the `detail` is printed for every check (briefs.rs:1449-1460), and that `Git::ls_tree` exists (athena-git lib.rs:516). The test fixtures the plan names also exist: `leaked_sh_check`, `run_checked_job`, `recording_verifier_prompts`, `commit_file`, `editing`, the `probe` check name, and `job_with_checks`/`check` in reading.rs. The demonstrations use real seams with no test doubles. The fix to resolve cited tokens against tracked files is sound. One dependent effect is missed: `judge` puts Athena's check findings before the verifier's findings, and `athena-cli` display.rs:985 prints only the first five findings of a rejected job. Adding one more Minor finding per failing check can push verifier and Major findings off the owner's screen, and no test covers this. Two smaller design points follow. First, the route facts, which the plan itself calls the part that separates cases, are shown only when a tracked path is cited. Second, the change description departs from criterion 1's wording without saying how the two relate.
